results.notes: This dataset is a customization of Statistics Canada data to present information on labour force survey estimates by sex, age groups, education level, and immigrant status in Canada and provinces for 2018 using annual averages. The labour force characteristics presented on are population, full-time and part-time employment, unemployment, participation rate, and employment rate.
results.title: Labour force estimates by sex, age groups, education level, immigrant status, Canada and provinces (annual average) (2018)
topic: Education - Post - Secondary and Skills Training
results.usage:
- Labour Force Survey data are collected by Statistics Canada and are used to produce the well-known unemployment rate as well as other standard labour market indicators such as the employment rate and the participation rate. The Labour Force Survey also provides employment estimates by industry, occupation, public and private sector, hours worked and much more, all cross-classifiable by a variety of demographic characteristics. Estimates are produced for Canada, the provinces, the territories and a large number of sub-provincial regions. For employees, data on wage rates, union status, job permanency and establishment size are also produced.

- More information about the Labour Force Survey can be found on the Statistics Canada website, at https://www23.statcan.gc.ca/imdb/p2SV.pl?Function=getSurveyandSDDS=3701.

results.notes: Regional Collaborative Service Delivery (RCSD) is a new way to more effectively meet the learning needs of children and youth and support their well-being. The purpose of this approach is to ensure children and youth have aligned and co-ordinated access to supports and services they need to be successful in school and in their community. Regional Collaborative Service Delivery is a joint endeavour of Alberta Education, Alberta Health, Alberta Human Services and Alberta Health Services. It enables partners to work together on a regional basis to enhance the supports and services of identified children, youth, and their families within the context of their home, school and community.

results.notes: This guide outlines the provincial requirements for school board three-year education plans and annual education results reports. It details the mandatory elements, including mission, vision, goals, desired results, performance measures, targets, strategies, and financial reporting. The guide also explains the linkages between provincial and school board planning, the review process by Alberta Education, and submission deadlines for these documents. It aims to ensure continuous improvement in education and inform Albertans about the quality and priorities of the education system.

results.name: guide-for-developing-the-november-1995-school-board-annual-education-report
results.notes: This guide assists school boards in completing their November 1995 Annual Education Report. It outlines the 1995 reporting requirements for school boards and establishes timelines for implementing results reporting, reflecting the government's Accountability in Education Policy Framework—June 1995. The guide details the responsibilities of Alberta Education, school boards, and schools within the accountability relationship and describes the provincial education accountability cycle. It also specifies the mandatory information to include in the report, such as priorities, expenditure summaries, programs offered, and student achievement results.

results.name: annual-report-diploma-examinations-program-0163310073156
results.notes: This document summarized province-wide results from Alberta's Grade 12 Diploma Examinations Program for each school year, combining data from multiple sittings. It presented analyses of student achievement by course, gender, and population subgroup, along with participation rates and achievement trends over time. It outlined examination development and marking processes, offered guidance for interpreting results, and highlighted key factors influencing performance. The document helped educators, parents, administrators, researchers and policymakers assess outcomes and inform continuous improvement in Alberta's education system.
